newsitem.title: USA: American pilots make new pay offer to avert strike.
newsitem.headline: American pilots make new pay offer to avert strike.

text.p: The American Airlines pilots' union said Thursday it made a new proposal on pay to try to avert a strike set for midnight Friday against the nation's No. 2 carrier.

The union's chief negotiator, Brian Mayhew, said the proposal was made late Wednesday during joint negotiations with American. "We have been working that issue through the mediation board," which is overseeing the negotiations, he added. Another union spokesman said there has been no response from American.
The pay proposal was the latest in a series of offers between the two sides.

The union had proposed an 11.5 percent pay increase over four years, with American countering with 4 percent. Earlier this week, American increased its offer to 6 percent, but withdrew one of two stock options it had previously included.
The pilots rejected the 6 percent offer and the withdrawal of a second stock option, saying its overall effect was a package reduced in value by $43.1 million.

Union spokesmen said they remained frustrated at the pace of the talks, saying "the clock is ticking." Another repeated a union statement made several times earlier this week that "a strike is more likely than not."
A union spokesman told reporters, "We're not that far apart" on terms for a new contract.
The most contentious issues between the union and American are pay and what pilots would fly the new smaller jets the airline intends to buy for its regional airline, American Eagle.

American wants to have lower-paid Eagle pilots from another union fly them, while the Allied Pilots Association wants its members to fly the aircraft. American has said it needed the lower-paid pilots in order to be competitive with other major carriers which have low-cost regional airline services.
The union late last night made an offer to accept lower pay for its members who would fly the smaller jets, provided the jets flew under the "American Airlines" banner and not that of Eagle.
